findings.description: Critical: lifecycle rebuilding requires a valid cache for every surviving store file before publishing any prune. A scoring failure deliberately leaves newly admitted stubs in the store without caches; if an older ranked stub is then approved or rejected, the next preflight reaches the cache-less survivor, raises, and cannot prune the terminal item or perform the required later scoring retry.
findings.resolution: Make lifecycle rebuild tolerate store entries that were never part of the prior digest: rebuild the maintained prior digest from the intersection of prior ranked items and valid prior caches, preserve unscored survivors for the subsequent scoring retry, and add a regression covering failed scoring followed by a terminal decision.

findings.description: Critical: the promised `--force` same-fingerprint cache reuse has no executable path. `prepare-batch` always uses the new cycle `as_of`, while `rank` without a score document rejects every prior singleton whose `scored_at` differs from that new value; the documented Rank sequence otherwise dispatches an analyst unconditionally. Thus a forced unchanged cycle either dispatches contrary to the spec or fails cache validation instead of re-presenting the prior digest.
findings.resolution: Add an explicit cache-reuse/digest-reuse command or branch that validates requested-key composition, prior digest fingerprint, singleton key identity, and original `generated_at` without requiring old `scored_at` to equal the new cycle time; pin it with an end-to-end forced-cycle test.

findings.description: Critical: mutating commands recover a pending transaction after the host has already rehydrated and supplied `record`, then continue using that pre-recovery record. A recovered mirror can therefore be overwritten later in the same cycle by stale gates, decisions, or digested-stub state, violating the requirement to preserve unrelated newer durable state.
findings.resolution: Make recovery a distinct pre-rehydration host step, or require a command that recovered state to stop and instruct the host to rehydrate/restart. Alternatively merge the recovered mirror with the supplied record using the canonical timestamp authority before any subsequent publication. Add an interrupted-rank-to-next-cycle regression.

findings.description: Critical: `rank` never binds its manifest candidates to the current persisted store. A stale manifest can publish caches and a digest for old candidate bytes after a same-key refresh; because candidate outputs are excluded from the cycle fingerprint, the mismatch can then be reused indefinitely on an unchanged tree.
findings.resolution: Before accepting scores, validate that every manifest candidate byte-for-byte matches the current candidate store (or the validated dry-run overlay) and that the key sets agree. Use a cycle lock or expected-store digest to close the prepare-to-rank race, with a regression that refreshes a same-key candidate between those calls.

findings.description: Critical: an empty surviving backlog yields a valid-looking manifest with zero requested keys, but the rubric schema requires at least one score and the workflow says to dispatch exactly one analyst. There is no successful first-cycle or changed-cycle path for the ordinary case where discovery produces no candidates.
findings.resolution: Specify and implement a zero-candidate fast path that skips analyst dispatch and emits or reuses a schema-valid empty candidate digest, then add workflow and runtime tests for an initially empty store and for a backlog becoming empty after terminal pruning.

findings.description: none: transaction recovery now authorizes operation-specific supervisor-owned paths, bounds bytes and operation count, validates every entry and checksum before mutation, and keeps digest replacement last.
findings.resolution: Retain the complete-preflight and target-authorization regressions.

findings.description: none: model dispatch remains in the host skill while the new runtime is deterministic and network-free, and approval continues through the preview/SHA-guarded refiner boundary rather than writing roadmap YAML directly.
findings.resolution: Preserve the host-assisted boundary and the no-roadmap-write structural tests.
